About Me

Planning for people,rooted in community.

I'm an urban planner and project manager with experience spanning community planning, public space advocacy, and equitable development. My work is grounded in a simple belief: that cities thrive when the people who live in them have a real voice in shaping them.

From leading participatory design research at UC San Diego's Design Lab to studying public space use in Detroit's Planning & Development Department, I've built my career around listening first, then planning. I bring both the analytical rigor of a planner and the people-centered instincts of a community organizer.

My academic work on equitable smart growth and gentrification deepened my understanding of how planning decisions — well-intentioned or not — can uplift or displace communities. That awareness drives everything I do.

Academic Work

Research rooted inreal communities.

Equitable Smart Growth Practices in Urban Communities: Highlighting the Power of Collaborative City Planning
Senior Research Proposal  ·  USP 187 — Urban Studies & Planning, UC San Diego  ·  2020

This research explored how non-profit organizations and collaborative planning frameworks have shaped underrepresented urban communities — examining the intersection of gentrification, cultural displacement, and the erasure of identity in low-income communities of color. The study investigated how equitable smart growth, when done with communities rather than to them, can bridge economic disparities and create lasting opportunity for current and future residents.

Creative Cities Gentrification Urban Planning Smart Cities Collaborative Planning Equitable Development Displacement
🏙️
Smart Growth & Displacement
Analyzed how smart growth initiatives, while well-intentioned, can accelerate displacement of low-income communities of color when not designed with equity at the center.
🤝
Collaborative Planning Power
Examined how non-profit organizations and community-led planning models have successfully leveraged local relationships to induce sustainable, community-rooted economic growth.
🌱
Cultural Preservation
Argued that sustaining the socio-cultural presence of a community provides hope, equity of access, and bridges economic disparities for both current and future residents.
